edges.reason: A room type belongs to a property.
A room belongs to a room type.
A rate plan prices a room type.
Restrictions attach to a rate plan.
Availability is counted from physical rooms.
Sellable availability is quoted against a rate plan.
A reservation can only be made against available inventory.

Can reuse a generic slot/date-range availability engine instead of bespoke room-inventory logic; not required, since room-type capacity and rate-plan restrictions are domain-specific enough to stand alone, as both inspected implementations do.
Confirmation and pre-arrival messages.
Check-in/out transitions an existing reservation.
Checkout can settle a single invoice without a full itemized folio, as Frappe Hospitality does.
A guest profile can be a full user account or a lightweight record captured at booking.
Settling a folio requires payment capture.
ARI sync pushes real inventory/rate data.
Channel bookings create internal reservations.
Deposit capture goes through a payment provider.
A cancellation policy is evaluated against a reservation's cancellation.
Refund calculation typically applies to a collected deposit; policies can also apply to pay-at-property bookings with nothing collected yet.
An add-on is attached to a reservation.
Charges post to a folio where one exists; can also settle directly on a single invoice.
A voucher documents a confirmed reservation.
Connecting rooms are a relationship between room records.
Managing several properties from one account needs a tenant/branch model.
Tasks are tracked against a room.
Checkout typically triggers a turnover task; housekeeping can also run on a fixed schedule.
The audit posts and reconciles folio charges.
Also resolves no-shows, but core posting/reconciliation works without that step.
A group booking is a reservation covering multiple rooms.
Loyalty accrues against a guest profile.
Reviews are typically requested post-stay; can also be collected without gating on checkout data.
Dynamic pricing adjusts an underlying rate plan.
